1. In a suit for declaration of title, where the plaintiff claims that he is the owner of the property bearing Survey No.236/2017 measuring 01 acre 19 guntas, situated in Turmari Village, Taluk Bailhongal, the plaintiff also moved an application for temporary injunction to restrain the defendants from withdrawing the compensation amount.

The compensation amount is determined by the Land Acquisition Officer, as the portion of the suit property i.e.,33 guntas of land is acquired under the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act of 2013', for short).

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. The entire case of the plaintiff is based on the premise that he purchased the suit property in the year 1952 and at the time of purchase, the property is wrongly numbered as Survey No.55/1 in the sale deed, instead of Survey No.55/17.

It is his case that, the NC: 2023:KHC-D:12322 defendants'
predecessor in title purchased some property in the year 1957 from the same vendor and the property said to have been purchased by the predecessor in title of the defendants also measures 01 acre 19 guntas.
It is further stated that, the boundaries are not provided in both the sale deeds.
Later two villages have been merged and after the merger of two villages, the property purchased by the plaintiff is renumbered as 236/17.
3. The defendants disputed the plaintiff's claim.

The defendants contended that the plaintiff purchased Survey No.55/1 and not 55/17 and merely because the extent of both the lands are identical as per the description provided in the sale deed, it cannot be said that the plaintiff has purchased the very property purchased by the predecessor in title of the defendants.

The application is not filed and the steps are not taken for rectification of the sale deed till NC: 2023:KHC-D:12322 today and only after the acquisition of the land by the authority, the plaintiff has filed the frivolous case.
4. Learned counsel appearing for the plaintiff/appellant Sri. Srinivas B. Naik would urge that the order dismissing the application seeking temporary injunction is impermissible.

The prima facie case is made out by the plaintiff, as the original sale deed is produced and it is also shown that the plaintiff's vendor has sold the property to the predecessor in title of the defendants and the property measuring 01 acre 19 guntas is sold.
Thus, he would contend that the vendor of the predecessor in title of the defendants had no right to alienate the property which is already sold to the plaintiff.

He would also submit that, in case the compensation amount is withdrawn by the defendants, the plaintiff will be put to irreparable loss and injury and in case the plaintiff succeeds, the recovery becomes difficult and the plaintiff can not realize the fruits of the decree.

sentences.text: 3 5. Sri. Dinesh M. Kulkarni, learned counsel appearing for the defendants would urge that, the trial Court has considered all relevant aspects of the matter and has rightly concluded that the plaintiff has no prima facie case and rightly refused the relief of temporary injunction sought by the plaintiff.

He would submit that the sale deed produced by the plaintiff does not refer to the property bearing Survey No.55/17 measuring 1 acre 19 guntas purchased by the predecessor in title of the defendants and if at the plaintiff has purchased any property from the vendor of the predecessor in title of the defendants, the said property is survey No.55/1 and steps have not been taken to rectify the error, if any, in the description of the property from 1952 onwards and it is self-evident that the property purchased is survey No.55/1 and not Survey No.55/17.
6.
This Court has considered the contentions raised at the Bar.
There is no dispute that 33 guntas in the suit property is acquired under the Act of 2013 and compensation is determined.
The compensation is not yet released in favour of the persons in whose favour the award is passed.
The suit is filed claiming declaration of title in respect of Survey No.236/17.
The claim of the plaintiff is to be established during the course of the trial.
The trial Court has concluded that the plaintiff has not made out a prima facie case.

8. The scope of the Appellate Court in exercise of power under Order XLIII Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure is limited in the sense the Appellate Court will not interfere with the discretionary orders passed on an interlocutory application, as the rights of the parties are not yet finally decided at this stage.
However, in appropriate cases, the Court may intervene in the order to balance the equities.

In this case, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant and respondents that the compensation is NC: 2023:KHC-D:12322 already determined and the compensation is about to be released in favour of the defendants in whose favour the award is passed.

Though the award is in the name of dependents and the payment should ordinarily be made in favour of the award holder,
in view of the contentions raised, this Court is of the view that the defendants should be put on certain terms before disbursing the compensation amount in their favour.

9. To ensure that the plaintiff is not put to difficulty in realizing the fruits of the decree, in case the plaintiff succeeds, this Court is of the view that the compensation amount determined in respect of 33 guntas of land in the suit property, be released in favour of the defendants, subject to the defendants furnishing an undertaking before the trial Court that the defendants will deposit the compensation amount along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of receipt till the date of deposit, within three NC: 2023:KHC-D:12322 months from the date of the decree, in case the decree is passed holding that the plaintiff is entitled to the said compensation amount.
10.
In case the undertaking, as above, is not furnished, the compensation amount shall not be released in favor of the defendants.
11. It is further made clear that, this Court has not expressed any opinion on the merits of the suit.

The trial Court shall decide the suit without being influenced by any of the observations made in this Prakash Ramchandra Pawar vs Sri. Rudrappa Irappa Totagi on 12 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196737044/
